This document outlines the contact system check to be done for 
 circuit breaker up to 50 KV rated short circuit breaking current every time 
 the circuit breaker is operated (open or close ) the contact system is 
 subjected to mechanical or electrical stress.

The electrical stress is evident by virtue of erosion on the components. The 
 intensity of thus erosion depends on the amplitude of the current switched 
 with frequent switching and / or high breaking currents, the stress dependant 
 wear determines. The point in time when a contact system check must be 
 implemented:

Lift thed- interrupter unit far enough (max. 200mm ) so that the spacer W350 
 (fig. 1 page 5-0150/2) (L= 170 mm ) fit between it and post insulator . then 
 screw the studs of the spacer in the threaded holes of cement flange of the 
 interrupter unit. Now lower the interrupter unit gently onto the studs and 
 guide the studs through the bore hoks in the cement of the interrupter unit. 
 Put the nut on the ends of the studs and use them to screw the cement flange 
 down onto the spacer.

Undo the nut, remove the spacing discs if 
 fitted (fig. 3) and keep them in a safe place for reassembly.

sections.text: Removing the Blast Module and the moving contact system

items: Remove the screws fixing the flange plate (22.33) to the porcelain jacket

Mark the position of the flange plate on the cement flange of the interrupter 
 unit.

Avoid damage the blast cylinder; damage the cylinder may impair the quenching 
 process. This may lead to damage or destruction to the circuit break pull 
 out the flange plate with the lower terminal plate (22.22) and the blast 
 cylinder (22.05), fix this module on a firm support horizontally (fig. 4)

Mark the position of the blast cylinder ()22.05) with respect to the 
 flange plate . remove the four screws (22.23.1 ) , and then withdraw the blast 
 cylinder from the moving contact tube (22.7) so that the locking bolts 
 (22.7.5 ) come free (fig . 4).

Undo the nuts (22.13.12 ) from the three studs of the filter to enable the 
 "blast cylinder complete" module to be removed . do not dismantle this module 
 any further (fig. 4).

To detach the moving contact tube (22.7 fig.5 ), remove the bolts (22.7.5) and take out the fork (16. 9.1). Withdraw the moving contact tube from the 
 guide tube (22.11).

When the moving contact tube has been removed, undo the four screws from the 
 guide tube and replace the tube.
The moving contact tube and the blast cylinder must be replaced in pairs.

The interrupter unit is assembled in reverse order as described for 
 dismantling with due attention to marks provided during dismantling.

Smooth the contact face of the flange plate with a brush only used for copper 
 surfaces and apply a thin film of acid free Vaseline. Screw down the guide 
 tube and grease its out side with a very thin film of centoplex 24 DL.

Slide the moving contact tube (22.7) over the guide tube in such a manner that 
 the boreholes for the bolt (22.7.5 ) and the slots of the moving contact tube 
 are in line .enter the fork (16.9.1) from the flange (22.23) plate and 
 fix to the moving contact tube by means of bolt (22.7.5). Make sure the 
 centering pin (16.9.5) has the correct position with respect to the 
 lower terminal plate (22.22)

Apply a very thin film of the centoplex 24 DL to the outer cylinder surface of 
 the moving contact tube(22.7). plug the assembled( blast cylinder complete) 
 nodule with the studs through the borehole of the moving contact, making sure 
 that it fits properly , and screw down to the flange plate (22.23) . slide the 
 blast cylinder(22.5) over the moving contact tube. following this mount the 
 porcelain jacket (22.1) and measure the centre offset.

sections.text:
Measuring the 
Free Gas Path 
and the Centre offset

After replacement of the contact and guide 
 tubes , the free gas path and the centre offset must be measured .

items:
Using a depth gauge ( measuring range ≥ 1000mm ), determine clearance "b" 
 between plate (22.31) and arc quenching nozzle (22.9.1 fig. 8 page 5- 
 0150/6).

Likewise by means of a depth gauge , determine clearance "c" between sealing 
 surface of the porcelain jacket and the blast cylinder ( 22.5 
 fig .4 page 
 5-0150/3 )
The difference between "b" and "c" is the clearance in gas.

The nominal dimension (e.g 20,30, or 40mm) is subject to a tolerance of -2/+3 
 mm if this tolerance is exceeded, the approved free gas path must be 
 reestablished by exchanging the parts.

Mount the plate kowl (22.31) with the contact tube and the contact tube 
 support.

Remove the cover from the plate kowl and fit mounting plate 1 . in its place 
 . Introduce the rod 2 . through the mounting plate .

The front end of the rod is fitted with a spike that matches the inside 
 diameter of the nozzle.

With the approved centre offset, the spike can be pushed into the graphite 
 nozzle of the guide tube .

Like all other special tools, the centre offset testing device W371 can be 
 obtained on loan from the filed services department ANL A4 erlangen.
